senses.def: be undecided about something; waver between conflicting positions or courses of action
ex: He oscillates between accepting the new position and retirement

senses.def: move or swing from side to side regularly
ex: the needle on the meter was oscillating

senses.def: having periodic vibrations
the process of oscillating between states
(physics) a regular periodic variation in value about a mean
a single complete execution of a periodically repeated phenomenon
electronic equipment that provides visual images of varying electrical quantities
(biology, chemistry) diffusion of molecules through a semipermeable membrane from a place of higher concentration to a place of lower concentration until the concentration on both sides is equal
appearing as such but not necessarily so
ex: the ostensible truth of their theories

senses.def: represented or appearing as such; pretended
ex: His ostensible purpose was charity, his real goal popularity

senses.def: from appearances alone
ex: had been ostensibly frank as to his purpose while really concealing it

senses.def: a gaudy outward display
lack of elegance as a consequence of being pompous and puffed up with vanity
intended to attract notice and impress others
with ostentation; in an ostentatious manner
ex: Mr Khrushchev ostentatiously wooed and embraced Castro at the U.N. general assembly

senses.def: the state of being banished or ostracized (excluded from society by general consent)
the act of excluding someone from society by general consent
expel from a community or group
avoid speaking to or dealing with
ex: Ever since I spoke up, my colleagues ostracize me

senses.def: a person who refuses to face reality or recognize the truth (a reference to the popular notion that the ostrich hides from danger by burying its head in the sand)
fast-running African flightless bird with two-toed feet; largest living bird
